{{Quote|We need more Effex droids. I've put in this requisition three times. Every day you delay, clone troopers die.|[[Jos Vondar]]|<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
The '''FX-series medical assistant droid''', also referred to as '''Fixits''', was a [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]] series line produced by [[Medtech Industries/Legends|Medtech Industries]]. There were multiple models and they were often immobile, cylindrical [[Droid/Legends|droids]] with numerous [[Manipulator arm/Legends|arms]] that assisted patients during surgery or other medical procedures. FX-series droids were originally meant to assist organic [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]], but soon began working in tandem with specialized surgical droids such as the [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B]].

==Description==
The FX-series was designed with utility in mind; each unit was symmetrical and cylindrical and no attempt was made to make it look [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]].<ref name="EGTD" /> Nine separate models were produced that shared a basic design, ranging from the [[FX-1 medical assistant droid|FX-1]] to the [[FX-9 surgical assistant/Legends|FX-9]].<ref name="NEGTD" /> The units were not designed to be mobile<ref name="EGTD" /> as it was assumed that they would be stationed in operating theaters.<ref name="NEGTD" /> FX droids either had to be physically dragged from one location to another<ref name="EGTD" /> or ferried on [[Repulsorcart/Legends|repulsorcarts]]. The [[FX-6 medical assistant droid|FX-6 model]] had a trio of casters built into the bottom allowing it to roll.<ref name="NEGTD" />

The cap-shaped head of the FX-series was capable of rotating a full three hundred and sixty degrees, and was fitted with [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]], medical [[Medical scanner/Legends|diagnostic sensors]], and a [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]] port.<ref name="EGTD" /> Some models were fitted with a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] that could communicate only in droid or [[Computer/Legends|computer]] [[Language/Legends|languages]].<ref name="NEGTD" /> All FX-series droids had an [[Analytical computer/Legends|analytical computer]] and medical diagnostic package installed and their efficiency could be increased if they were connected to a [[Medical droid/Legends|surgical droid]] or medical mainframe via the scomp link. Monitor screens were installed on the head and upper body that could display information, charts, graphs and schematics,<ref name="EGTD" /> and could also be used to transmit the FX's thoughts in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

The majority of the [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] body was comprised of [[Manipulator arm/Legends|manipulator arms]] on a rotating base. The standard number of arms was twenty,<ref name="EGTD" /> although this could vary and number anywhere between five and twenty-five on individual modules. The arms were interchangeable and removable,<ref name="NEGTD" /> and they laid flat in a protective groove when not in use. Each was equipped with a variety of implements such as grippers, medical tools,<ref name="EGTD" /> [[Hypodermic injector/Legends|injectors]], and [[Breath mask/Legends|gas masks]]<ref name="AEG">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> that could be swapped out to better suit the medical environment the droid was operating in.<ref name="NEGTD" /> The limbs were lightweight and easy to damage, but since FX droids were not expected to operate in rough conditions, this was not considered to be a drawback.<ref name="EGTD" />

The droid's primary [[Grasper arm/Legends|grasping arm]] was situated at the top of the FX's torso above the manipulator arms. Capable of reaching up to one [[Meter/Legends|meter]], the arm was sturdy and used for everyday work.<ref name="EGTD" /> The [[FX-7 medical assistant droid/Legends|FX-7]] had one arm, while the FX-6 boasted seven arms.<ref name="NEGTD" />

==History==
[[File:FXmed_egtd.png|thumb|right|180px|FX medical assistant droid [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
Manufactured by [[Medtech Industries/Legends|Medtech Industries]], the FX-series was designed to serve as a surgical assistant, although it was often marketed as a general nursing assistant.<ref name="NEGTD" /> The droid was intended to assist organic [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]] in performing medical procedures where they were commonly used to administer [[Anesthetic gas|anesthesia]] to patients, monitor their vital signs during surgery, and provide the physician with the necessary medical tools to complete the procedure.<ref name="EGTD" /> After their release, they were considered to be one of the greatest additions to the field of medicine since the discovery of [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]].<ref name="AEG" />

With the release of dedicated surgical droids such as the [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B surgical droid]], FX droids were retasked to work in tandem with them as well.<ref name="NEGTD" /> However, the introduction of such surgical droids reduced the need for specialized medical aides. Despite receiving few complaints about the droid's performance, Medtech eventually retired the line<ref name="EGTD" /> after [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of dedicated service.<ref name="NEGTD" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] forces often deployed FX-series droids at their [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit/Legends|Republic Mobile Surgical Units]]. FX droids were part of the duty staff at the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] where an FX-6 unit assisted with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] transformation into Darth Vader.<ref name="NEGTD" /> When Palpatine informed Vader that he had killed [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], his fit of rage and grief caused the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] to destroy everything in the room with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], including the medical droids. The head of the FX model that worked on Vader was crushed, as well most of its body.<ref name="ROTS">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]</ref>

By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the FX-series was considered to be obsolete. However, they were still common throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and found on thousands of [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansions Region]] and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] used FX droids extensively and they made excellent [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] operators with the correct programming, with many used by both the [[Xucphra Corporation|Xucphra]] and [[Zaltin Corporation]]s on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]].<ref name="EGTD" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|The second edition of ''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']] incorrectly states that the FX series comprised only nine models.

In the [[Battlefront]] series, FX medical droids act as health-replenishing stations that automatically heal players whenever they stand nearby.

===Toy versions of FX droids===
The FX first appeared in the vintage 3 3/4-inch [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] line in 1980. Released on the new ''The Empire Strikes Back'' cards, FX-7 is a unique figure in the original line, consisting of a gray tubular body and a head that can be spun 360 degrees and extended upwards by an inch. Underneath the head is a rigid white arm terminating in a claw appendage. This arm is mounted on a spinning ring, allowing it to be spun 360 degrees around the body. The main part of the body has nine white arms that can be opened out away from the body. Although these limbs have no joints, they can be slightly articulated at the elbow and shoulder. There is a major variation with the FX-7 figure in that two different head molds exist. One head is smaller with differently situated detail from the other. Another shorter FX-7 can be found on card; this figure is simply missing its glued-on base that sometimes broke off during production. This shorter FX-7 is not classed as a true variation but merely a production mistake. FX-7 ran for five years through the ''Empire'', ''Jedi'' and Tri-logo line.

The next FX-7 figure to be released came in the Power Of The Jedi line in 2000&ndash;2002. This figure offers a far more realistic look and greater attention to detail than the vintage toy. Twice as many articulated limbs as the vintage figure, jointed at the elbow and shoulder, give it much more detail and capture a close likeness of the original production prop.
